value.gap_vs_onpoint: Vue.ai presents an enterprise AI platform with a fashion-forward capability (virtual dressing room and on-model imagery) that is gated behind a work-email/demo flow. Public evidence confirms a strong emphasis on model diversity, outfit composition, and retailer customization, but there is no public, self-serve try-on, no consumer-upload flow, no observable stock/price/checkout connected to the try-on experience, and pricing is not shown on the main site (pricing appears on a separate Shopify listing by a different developer). This creates a gap for OnPoint: whereas OnPoint can directly tie fit-aware visualization to live stock, local-pay, and agent-enabled procurement, Vue.ai remains anchored to an enterprise-clarity narrative with gated access and a separate commerce path. A concrete OnPoint-oriented rewrite would emphasize verifiable stock provenance, local-pay rails, and agent-driven purchasing that bridges the visualization to actual checkout. See annotated evidence: landing/o-model entry/blocker/pricing/mobile/dev-docs/api-reference images.
value.pricing_tiers: Public pricing visible only on a separate Shopify listing (Starter $20/mo, Professional $35/mo, Business $75/mo); enterprise Vue.ai pricing not published on the main site. The Shopify listing lists a 3-day trial and identifies the developer as Duma, indicating adjacent-but-separate pricing surfaces.

value.value_proposition: Vue.ai markets an enterprise AI platform for orchestration with a focus on virtual dressing room capabilities. Public shopper-facing proof of a real try-on is blocked by a demo gate, reducing verifiability of exact garment-on-you outputs. The platform emphasizes model diversity, real-time styling, and retailer customization, but lacks a public, self-serve consumer trial path and integrated stock/pay flow—limiting direct evidence of in-stock purchasability tied to the try-on experience.
value.what_onpoint_should_copy: OnPoint should emphasize: (1) verifiable stock provenance and catalog linkage for each garment shown in a try-on, (2) a direct, local-pay-enabled checkout path (e.g., WhatsApp/M-Pesa) integrated to the same experience, (3) an Africa-curator graph (Ankara, Kente, Adire, Bogolan, Shweshwe, football-kit culture) that maps to real stock and fulfillment, and (4) a clear, consumer-appropriate try-on proof that does not misrepresent fit certainty.
